## Persistent allocation failure

The allocation probe `tests/native_allocation.cc` replaces every form of `operator new`. It sweeps every allocation of one encode and one decode. Direct `malloc` calls are outside the sweep. The wrapper has one, and it checks the result for null. In single mode, only the chosen allocation fails. In persistent mode, the chosen allocation and every later allocation fail. Each attempt runs in a child process, so the probe reports every terminating attempt and continues. The probe uses four configurations: a bit-count triangle, grid positions with unit-square texture coordinates, bit-count positions with fitted texture coordinates, and lossless positions with unit-square texture coordinates.

On the old pin (618e9bf), the persistent sweep has 119 terminating attempts, all with SIGABRT. All 119 backtraces end in `RAnsBitEncoder::~RAnsBitEncoder`, which calls `Clear`, which allocates. Two owners hold the encoder: `MeshEdgebreakerEncoderImpl` (117 attempts) and `MeshPredictionSchemeTexCoordsPortableEncoder::EncodePredictionData` (2 attempts). Decode never terminates. The cause is one destructor, so a local patch is sufficient.

The fork branch `fix/rans-bit-encoder-destructor` (673ee67) removes the `Clear` call from the destructor. `third_party/draco/CONSTRUKTED-CHANGES.md` documents the patch. With the patch, the probe has 0 defects in both modes. Every failed attempt returns an error and publishes no output.

In single mode, three attempts succeed although an allocation failed. In each, `std::stable_sort` requests a temporary buffer with nothrow `new`, gets none, and sorts in place. The encoded bytes are identical to the control encode. The probe counts these attempts as recovered, not as defects.

The patch does not change encoded output. A separate tool encodes every corpus primitive in five configurations: grid positions, grid positions with texture coordinates at 11 and at 16 bits, 14-bit positions with 10-bit texture coordinates, and lossless positions with 10-bit texture coordinates. 4,650 of 4,650 encoded buffers are byte-identical before and after the patch, and on the final source.

## Sanitizer runs

GCC cannot build with `-fsanitize=address,undefined` on .212. The GCC sanitizer runtimes are not installed: the linker reports that `/usr/lib64/libasan.so.8.0.0` and `/usr/lib64/libubsan.so.1.0.0` do not exist. The sanitized build uses clang 22.1.5 with compiler-rt instead. Stable Rust cannot instrument Rust code, so only the C++ code is instrumented. Rust links the sanitizer runtime through clang.

Sanitized build settings:

```sh
export CC=clang CXX=clang++
SAN="-fsanitize=address,undefined,float-divide-by-zero -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g --target=x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu"
export CFLAGS="$SAN" CXXFLAGS="$SAN"
export RUSTFLAGS="-C linker=clang++ -C link-arg=-fsanitize=address,undefined,float-divide-by-zero -C link-arg=--target=x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu"
cargo test --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
```

The `cc` crate passes `--target=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` to clang. Fedora installs compiler-rt under `x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu`, so the later `--target` flag selects the installed runtime. `nm` shows sanitizer calls in both `libdraco.a` and `libtileforge_draco.a`.

Results with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer:

1. `cargo test` passes. No sanitizer report.
2. `cargo test --release` passes. No sanitizer report.
3. The corpus gate passes in 1,214 seconds. No sanitizer report.
4. The allocation probe has 0 defects in both modes. No sanitizer report.

The sanitized runs found three problems outside Draco.

1. The build script put Draco before the C entry point on the link line. GNU ld resolves a static library only against the inputs before it, so the unit-test binary did not link. rust-lld, the default linker of Rust 1.94.1, accepts either order and hid the defect. With `-C link-arg=-fuse-ld=bfd`, `cargo test --release` fails before the fix and passes after it.
2. The probe did not replace the nothrow forms of `operator new`. AddressSanitizer supplies its own, and the probe released that memory with `free`. AddressSanitizer reported `alloc-dealloc-mismatch (operator new vs free)`. The probe now replaces the nothrow forms.
3. Clang warns `'BuildMesh' has C-linkage specified, but returns user-defined type 'std::unique_ptr<draco::Mesh>' which is incompatible with C [-Wreturn-type-c-linkage]`. `BuildMesh` is in an anonymous namespace inside the `extern "C"` block. It has internal linkage and only C++ calls it. This is a warning, not a defect, and this change does not move the function.

Clang also warns in Draco: `geometry_attribute.h:401:25: implicit conversion from 'unsigned int' to 'float' changes value from 4294967295 to 4294967296 [-Wimplicit-const-int-float-conversion]`. The comparison is `in_value >= std::numeric_limits<OutT>::max()` for a float input and a 32-bit unsigned output. The largest binary32 value below 2^32 converts without overflow, so the rounded limit is still safe.

## Grid-domain guard

`tests/native_grid_domain.cc` calls the C entry point directly, so the Rust guard does not filter the input. It encodes and decodes one triangle per case under the sanitizers.

| Case | Guard | Native result under UBSan |
|---|---|---|
| Span of 2^30 values (-63 to 2^30 - 64) | accepted | clean, exact |
| Lowest signed 32-bit index | accepted | clean, exact |
| Highest binary32 index below 2^31 | accepted | clean, exact |
| Span of 2^30 + 1 values | refused | clean, exact |
| Span of 2^30 + 129 values | refused | `expert_encode.cc:310:36: runtime error: signed integer overflow: -2147483648 - 1 cannot be represented in type 'int'`; decode fails |
| Index 2^31 | refused | `expert_encode.cc:295:26: runtime error: 2.14748e+09 is outside the range of representable values of type 'int'`; `expert_encode.cc:295:40: runtime error: signed integer overflow: -2147483648 - 2147482624 cannot be represented in type 'int'` |
| `grid_domain.rs` positive | refused | `expert_encode.cc:295:26` and `295:59: runtime error: 4.096e+09 is outside the range of representable values of type 'int'` |
| `grid_domain.rs` negative | refused | `expert_encode.cc:295:26` and `295:59: runtime error: -4.096e+09 is outside the range of representable values of type 'int'` |
| `grid_domain.rs` span | refused | `expert_encode.cc:310:36: runtime error: signed integer overflow: -2147483648 - 1 cannot be represented in type 'int'`; decode fails |
| `grid_domain.rs` float max | refused | see below; decode fails |

The float-max case reports five errors:

```text
expert_encode.cc:295:26: runtime error: 3.40282e+38 is outside the range of representable values of type 'int'
quantization_utils.h:49:33: runtime error: 3.40282e+38 is outside the range of representable values of type 'int'
prediction_scheme_wrap_encoding_transform.h:60:43: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 0 - -2147483648 cannot be represented in type 'int'
stl_vector.h:1254:34: runtime error: applying non-zero offset 17179869180 to null pointer
stl_vector.h:1254:9: runtime error: reference binding to address 0x0003fffffffc with insufficient space for an object of type 'int'
```

The last two come from `draco::ComputeShannonEntropy`.

The data confirm the guard. The four `grid_domain.rs` cases and the two new edge cases reach undefined behaviour in Draco without the guard. The three accepted edge cases are clean and decode exactly. The guard is stricter than Draco at one point only: Draco counts the span values in binary32, which rounds 2^30 + 1 down to 2^30. The next binary32 count above 2^30 is 2^30 + 128, which needs 31 bits and overflows. `tests/grid_domain.rs` now checks the three accepted edges through the crate and refuses both new spans.

## Texture coordinates in the corpus gate

The TFGD dumps hold positions, triangle indices, and `TEXCOORD_0`. All 932 files hold texture coordinates, and every value is inside the unit square. The dumps hold no normals and no colors.

The gate now also encodes grid positions with unit-square texture coordinates at 10 to 16 bits. tileforge-optimize uses 10 bits. tileforge-mesh derives 11 to 16 bits from the atlas size. Draco can reorder vertices and faces and can rotate a face, but it keeps the winding. So the gate names each triangle corner by its own position and the positions of the next and previous corners. It checks both directions: each decoded corner must match an input corner within one quantization step, and each input corner must match a decoded corner.

930 primitives and 51,811,599 corners per bit depth pass. The worst error is 0.500030 steps at 10 bits and 0.501945 steps at 16 bits. A copy with a quarter-step tolerance fails on the first file at 0.4999995 steps, so the check measures the real error. The gate takes 403 seconds unsanitized, up from about 15 seconds.

To cover normals and colors, a dump needs per-vertex normals (three floats), per-vertex linear RGBA colors (four floats), and a flag for each. tileforge-mesh encodes normals at 10 bits and colors at 8 bits, both on Draco's fitted box. The renderer fidelity of any attribute is out of scope.

## Final gates

All on the final source, unsanitized:

```sh
cargo fmt --check
cargo test
cargo test --release
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --release --test grid_corpus -- --ignored --nocapture
```

All five commands exit with 0. The corpus gate passes in 372 seconds with the same worst errors as above. The allocation probe reports 0 defects. The grid-domain probe decodes the three accepted cases exactly. Without sanitizers, the float-max case stops with SIGSEGV, and the 2^30 + 129 span and the `grid_domain.rs` span fail to decode. The corpus byte comparison holds 4,650 of 4,650 identical buffers. A first run of the final gates found a `cargo fmt` difference in `tests/grid_corpus.rs`; the commit after it applies the rustfmt layout.

Standalone probe command, from the source directory:

```sh
ulimit -c 0
DRACO_NATIVE_BUILD=<target>/release/build/tileforge-draco-<hash>/out/build
g++ -std=c++17 -O1 -g -Ithird_party/draco/src -I"$DRACO_NATIVE_BUILD" -Ithird_party/draco/third_party/eigen tests/native_allocation.cc "$DRACO_NATIVE_BUILD/libdraco.a" -o native-allocation
./native-allocation
```

Select the build directory that holds `libdraco.a` and `draco_features.h`. Compile `tests/native_grid_domain.cc` the same way. For a sanitized probe, use `clang++` with the `SAN` flags above and the sanitized `libdraco.a`.

## Remaining limits

1. The fork branch `fix/rans-bit-encoder-destructor` exists only in a local clone. A consumer cannot fetch the pin until the branch is on the fork remote.
2. The allocation probe covers four small meshes. It does not prove recovery for every input.
3. The sanitizers instrument the C++ code only. Stable Rust cannot instrument the Rust code.
4. The corpus gate does not check normals or colors.
